page.layout: One printed page with two parallel columns of Hebrew-Latin lexicon entries. Left column first, top to bottom, then right column, top to bottom. Running heads at top left and top right. Page number at top right. Signature at bottom left, catchword at bottom right. No margin notes.

main_text.l: מְעַבְּדִים [?] facientes seruire,
Part. Hiph. pl. masc. Rad. עָבַד
מַעַבְּרִים [?] facientes transfire,
Part. Hiph. pl. masc. Rad. עָבַר
מַעַלֶיךָ [?] orbitæ tuæ, No. pl. m. aff. R. עָגַל
מְעָרָה [?] ornans se, Part. Hiph. f. m. R. עָרָה
מַעֲרָנִים [?] delicia, No. pl. m. R. עָרַן
מַעֲרֵד [?] sarculas, No. f. m. Rad. עָרַד ordinavit.
מַעֲוָּג [?] placenta, No. f. m. Rad. עָוַג placentas paravit.
מְעֻרָּד [?] statuminans, Part. Piel, f. m. R. עָרַד
מַעוֹז robur, מְעוּזִי meum, &c. No. f. m. aff. R. עָזַז roboravit.
מָעוּךְ compressus, מְעוּכָה compressa, Part. Pahul, f. m. fæm. Rad. מָעַךְ.
מָעֵל inique agens, Part. Piel, sing. m. à Rad. inusit. in Kal, עָלַל, sed
Piel, עָל.
מְעֻלָּל parvulus, No. Part. f. m. R. עָלַל.
habita- מָעוֹן, מְעוֹנָה, מְעוֹנִים [?] tio, מְעוֹנוֹת [?] habitationes, &c. No. f. & pl. m. & fæm. Rad. עוֹן tempus.
מְעֻנָּן [?] præstigiis utens,
præstigiator, Part. Piel, vel No. Part. f. m. Rad. עַיִן oculus.
מָשׁוּךְ [?] obscuratus, No. f. m. R. עוּךְ [?] lavit.
מְעוּפָּךְ [?] volans, Part. Piel, f. m. R. עוּף.
מְעוּרֵיהֶם [?] nuditates eo-
rum, No. pl. m. aff. Rad. עָרָה, sed forma, à עוּר.
מְעוֹת [?] scrupi, פְּמַעְתָּיו [?] sicut
scrupi ejus, No. pl. f. præf. aff. Rad. מָעָה.
מְעוּתָה [?] perversum, Part. Pual, f. m. R. עוּת.
מָעוֹז robur meum, מְעוֹז [?] e-
jus, מְעוּזָם [?] eorum, מְעוּזָם [?]

page.notes: Hebrew vocalisation and several Hebrew roots are blurred in the scan and are marked [?]. The catchword "robora," and signature "Ii 3" are at the foot. The running heads are read as "מ ע" on both sides; the left one is partly smudged. Some Latin words are read with some doubt (e.g. "statuminans", "delicia", "sarculas"). Entries wrap across printed lines; each printed line is given as its own line. The Hebrew of the word "habitatio" line and the "scrupi" line is uncertain.
